title: Vigil
subtitle: A self-funding liquidation guardian
bullets: Sells paid risk intelligence over x402
narration: AI agents can detect liquidation risk, but reliable execution is the hard last mile. Vigil is a self-funding Aave guardian. It monitors health, applies deterministic policy, rescues positions only through KeeperHub, sells the same intelligence to other agents over x four oh two, and proves every action.

title: The model cannot loosen policy
subtitle: Reasoning advises. Rules authorize.
narration: Vigil separates reasoning from authority. Deterministic code owns the health-factor threshold, cooldown, spend caps, and idempotency window. The language model has no allow field. It may only veto, reduce spending, or increase cooldown. Forty tests enforce that an advisory can never turn a policy denial into an onchain approval.

title: Health factor restored onchain
subtitle: Condition true → partial repay → verified state
narration: Here is the real rescue. KeeperHub read a health factor of one point one seven eight six, followed the true Condition branch, repaid Aave, and raised the position to one point five zero zero zero. The transaction was sponsored, confirmed on Sepolia, and recorded immediately with its KeeperHub execution ID and transaction hash.

title: Failures become evidence
subtitle: Classified retries, never blind repeats
narration: Autonomy without observability is unsafe. Vigil classifies gas, revert, nonce, RPC, and unknown failures from KeeperHub step logs. Retries use exponential backoff and stop after three attempts. If repayment succeeds but Telegram fails, Vigil alerts separately and never repays twice. The full rationale, logs, gas, before-and-after state, and transaction are sealed into a canonical SHA two fifty six receipt.

title: Risk intelligence becomes revenue
subtitle: Two read-only workflows · $0.02 per call
narration: Vigil funds itself by publishing two read-only products on the KeeperHub marketplace. Vigil risk check computes health factor, oracle price, liquidation-price scenario, and risk signals. Vigil rescue quote returns a nonnegative, debt-capped Aave repay plan. Both run against Aave Base and cost two cents per call.

title: Discover → challenge → pay → result
subtitle: KeeperHub agentic wallet pays Base USDC
narration: Now the money shot. A second minimal agent discovers Vigil risk check, verifies its typed MCP endpoint, and receives an HTTP four oh two challenge. KeeperHub's agentic wallet pays twenty thousand raw Base USDC. The workflow returns HTTP two hundred with execution V N five G, and Vigil independently confirms the matching USDC Transfer before appending it to the transaction ledger.

title: One agent. Seven execution surfaces.
subtitle: Useful today. Monetizable by agents. Auditable end to end.
narration: Vigil uses KeeperHub for direct execution, workflow orchestration, Aave actions, audit logs, marketplace MCP, x four oh two settlement, agentic wallet payment, and Telegram delivery. It is a working liquidation guardian, a paid agent service, and a detailed teardown of the exact friction between decision and dependable onchain action.
